conditions: Only Unicode apostrophe glyphs are normalized to ASCII apostrophe.
The apostrophe is retained as an internal token character.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT a dropped apostrophe unless a separate contextual rule proves the same lexeme.
decisions.reason: Curly and typographic apostrophes are encoding variants of the same written contraction or possessive. This does not authorize contraction expansion.

conditions: Match only a listed contraction with its exact auxiliary expansion.
Use a contiguous 1↔2 token span and preserve all surrounding tokens, order, and polarity.
The expansion must be unique for that contraction.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT if the contraction has another grammatical reading or if any neighboring token is missing or reordered.

modeConditions.vocabulary: Align only to the existing canonical/answers/source authority; paraphrases remain PARAPHRASE.
modeConditions.read: Match only the complete contiguous pair in order; preserve every other reference token and highlight reference indexes from the alignment.
modeConditions.cloze: The entire hidden target must be reproduced in place by the selected final utterance; all completeness and negation gates remain mandatory.
modeConditions.correction: Use the complete pair only; correction practice adds no scheduled SRS write.

decisions.reason: The enumerated fixed pairs preserve auxiliary, tense/aspect, and proposition. They are approved as grammatical variants, with separate provenance from Unicode/ASR spelling normalization.

conditions: Resolve ’s as is or has only when the complete local syntax admits exactly one standard parse.
Treat be + -ing and ’s been/’s got as candidate clues, not universal morphology rules.
Past-participle/adjective, ’s not, nominal, and possession collisions remain unresolved absent a complete parse.
decisions.failureAction: UNRESOLVED or REJECT; never choose is/has from ’s alone.

excludedModes.read: UNRESOLVED: context-dependent auxiliary parsing is outside the bounded exact-span policy.
excludedModes.cloze: UNRESOLVED: context-dependent auxiliary parsing is outside the hidden-target policy.

decisions.reason: He’s can be he is or he has; it’s can be it is, it has, or a possessive-shaped ASR collision. Examples such as He’s finished and He’s not finished admit materially different parses.
minimalCounterexample: Observed: he’s finished (also parses as he has finished)

conditions: Resolve ’d as had before an unambiguously past participle, or would before an unambiguously bare infinitive / fixed better-rather idiom.
Keep syncretic forms such as put, read, and cut unresolved without wider syntax.
Do not infer elided have in would have constructions.
decisions.failureAction: UNRESOLVED if the following construction does not force had or would.
decisions.reason: I’d may stand for I had or I would, and the auxiliary changes tense/aspect or modality.
minimalCounterexample: Expected: I would put it there
Observed: I’d put it there (had/would form collision without wider syntax)

conditions: Match only the exact listed auxiliary + not pair and its listed contraction.
The aligned span must contain the auxiliary and the negative marker together.
Preserve auxiliary identity, tense, order, and negation scope in both directions.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT if not/ n’t is absent, another auxiliary replaces it, or the negation is outside the matched span.

modeConditions.vocabulary: Align only to existing canonical/answers/source authority; a paraphrase is never promoted.
modeConditions.read: Match the complete auxiliary + negator pair contiguously and preserve the remainder of the reference.
modeConditions.cloze: The complete hidden target span must map in place; preservesExpectedNegation and completeness remain hard gates.
modeConditions.correction: Match the complete pair; do not add a scheduled SRS write.

decisions.reason: Listed pairs such as do not/don’t and will not/won’t differ in contraction but preserve the same auxiliary and negative polarity when matched as a whole pair.

conditions: Treat cannot/can’t as a listed fixed negative pair.
Do not automatically equate can not with cannot/can’t: split can not may scope over the following verb or express a choice not to act.
decisions.failureAction: UNRESOLVED for can not unless the intended narrow negative auxiliary construction is independently established.

excludedModes.cloze: UNRESOLVED pending scope and target policy.

decisions.reason: Spacing can affect scope: “I can not go” may mean I can choose not to go, while “I cannot go” denies ability or permission.
minimalCounterexample: Observed: I can not go (scope reading may differ)

conditions: Resolve let’s to let us only as a first-person plural hortative with a following base verb.
Do not equate with permission/request “let us …” without discourse evidence.
decisions.failureAction: UNRESOLVED when discourse force or construction is unclear.
decisions.reason: Let’s go is ordinarily hortative; let us go can instead request permission.
minimalCounterexample: Observed: Let us go (may request permission rather than propose action)

conditions: No automatic expansion. A dialect-specific speaker model and sentence parse would be required.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT for ASR-09B automatic equivalence; preserve as unresolved audit evidence.
decisions.reason: Ain’t can stand for several be/have forms, is dialect-marked, and does not have one stable auxiliary or register interpretation.
minimalCounterexample: Observed: she ain’t ready (negative polarity differs)

conditions: Do not expand lexical ’s as an auxiliary when followed by a possessed noun.
Any possessive/auxiliary collision requires complete syntax and reference context.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT the minimal auxiliary substitution; otherwise leave unresolved.
decisions.reason: John’s book contains a possessive marker. Treating ’s as is or has changes the structure and can invent an auxiliary.

conditions: The complete phrase uses ’s as a possessive determiner before a lexical noun.
Do not expand it to be/have or strip the possessive relation.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT auxiliary expansion for this observed span.
decisions.reason: The noun context determines possessive ’s, so an auxiliary expansion changes the syntactic relation.

conditions: Require context-specific lexical/grammatical evidence for were/we’re, your/you’re, their/they’re/there, and its/it’s.
Do not infer an apostrophe or auxiliary from sound alone.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT generic contraction/possessive or contraction/past-tense substitution.
decisions.reason: Several pairs are homophonous or close in common speech but have different grammatical roles and meanings.

conditions: Aren’t I is eligible only as the conventional negative tag after a first-person positive clause.
It is not a general spelling/contraction of am not.
decisions.failureAction: REJECT outside an interrogative tag with the matching antecedent polarity.
decisions.reason: “I am …, aren’t I?” is an idiomatic tag construction, not a local expansion pair with “am not”.

conditions: Negation marker and scope must be preserved in both directions.
decisions.failureAction: Reject; do not score or align the missing polarity marker as equivalent.
decisions.reason: Dropping or adding not changes polarity.

conditions: Auxiliary, tense/aspect, and modal force must remain the same.
decisions.failureAction: Reject; never use a contraction family to substitute a different auxiliary.
decisions.reason: The surface contraction must not conceal a swap such as is/has or would/had.

conditions: A contracted auxiliary must be licensed by its syntactic construction; do not assume an elided predicate at sentence end.
Accept a short answer only if that exact elliptical form is independently licensed.
decisions.failureAction: Reject unsupported terminal forms such as “Yes, he’s” for “Yes, he is”.
decisions.reason: Many contractions require a following predicate; expanding a terminal form may silently add omitted words.

conditions: Evaluate each finalized hypothesis independently.
Do not join words from rank 0, lower ranks, segments, or prior attempts.
decisions.failureAction: Reject a synthesized phrase that no provider hypothesis contained.
decisions.reason: A grammar resolver may only align a complete observed phrase; it cannot manufacture missing evidence from separate candidates.
minimalCounterexample: Rank 0: do / rank 2: not agree; neither is the complete expected phrase
